$comment: THE FROZEN ROUTING DENOMINATOR for the repair-vs-finding router.
A later change MUST NOT mint new members or edit these expectations to re-classify: the
proof is that this exact table scores the router, with nothing added to make it pass
(the treadmill law). A row
that stops catching what its rationale claims is a finding about the router, never a
reason to move the row.
WHAT A ROW IS. A row is a MEMBER SPEC -- eight fields describing one member test's run
evidence -- which the test builds into a real CompletedRunHandoff through the shared
builders in ../../evidence-fixtures.ts. Nothing here is a CompletedRunHandoff literal. A
corpus assembled as a type literal can pin an input no producer is able to emit, and a
mutation differential then reds only impossible fixtures, which cannot tell a vacuous
corpus apart from a real closure.
THE CONTROL SHAPE, which is the reason the table looks the way it does. A cell that
screens against an EMPTY suite leaves 'the lane admits' untested on the only input where
refusing was possible at all -- and a threshold that refused everything would pass the
whole file. So every row
except the signature cell declares itself a variant of another row by a NAMED set of
fields, and the corpus-integrity cell verifies that declaration mechanically against the
actual key-set difference. So every discriminating signal has a row on each side of it,
and the two rows differ in that signal ALONE.
THE PAIRS THIS BUYS, each crossing an arm boundary on one field:
clean-definitive-assertion-fail (FINDING)  vs  mechanics-termination        (REPAIR)
clean-definitive-assertion-fail (FINDING)  vs  mechanics-planning-failure   (REPAIR)
clean-definitive-assertion-fail (FINDING)  vs  historical-cycle             (FINDING)
clean-definitive-assertion-fail (FINDING)  vs  historical-stagnation        (FINDING)
passing-run                     (REFUSE)   vs  mechanics-member-timeout     (REPAIR)
passing-run                     (REFUSE)   vs  mechanics-member-cancelled   (REPAIR)
and the sharpest pair in the table, which differs in NO field at all except one integer:
mechanics-termination (infeasibleSteps [1], the failing step)     -> REPAIR
mixed-evidence        (infeasibleSteps [0], a different step)     -> FINDING
Same signal, same count, same everything; only WHERE it sits. A router whose mechanics
scan is narrowed to the failing step gives these two rows the same answer, and no other
cell in this file would notice.
WHY THREE ROWS POINT AT FINDING AND ONLY TWO CLASSES ARE REPAIR-SHAPED. The asymmetry:
a mis-filed test-wrong costs one human look, a mis-routed application bug gets iterated
into passing, and only the second is unrecoverable. Ambiguity therefore routes to finding.
The three finding-direction cells are named below.
measured/ rationale on every row records what was actually observed by
running the row through the shipped classifier, not what the table's author expected.

The second arm is `stop`. `cycle` and `stagnation` are not mechanics signals: their blocks survive only in older handoffs and are read as nothing, so historical-cycle and historical-stagnation route exactly like the signature cell (stop, clean-definitive-assertion-fail). The limit-stop rule is pinned by the limit-stop cells in router.test.ts, outside this table.

rows.rationale: SOLE CATCHER for: a clean definitive assertion-fail NEVER reaches the repair arm. THE PHASE'S SIGNATURE CELL. Step 1's verifier said no, the deterministic assertValue comparator produced that verdict, and no step carries a mechanics signal -- so nothing about this failure is about how the test ACTS, and 'repairing' it could only mean rewriting what it CLAIMS to match what the application showed. That is oracle capture by construction, and this is the one row that says so.
rows.measured: route stop, signalClass clean-definitive-assertion-fail, failurePoint step 1 with verdictSource assert-value; scanned 2 steps and found zero mechanics signals and no member-level one.

rows.rationale: SOLE CATCHER for: a typed infeasible termination ON the failing step is execution mechanics, and mechanics repair. It is the signature cell plus one field: the same failing step, the same verdict source, plus a termination block. The step could not be carried out at all, so there is no expectation to have been wrong about -- the draft's mechanics are what need work.
rows.measured: route repair, signalClass execution-mechanics, mechanics [{stepIndex 1, termination}], failingStepIndex 1; the clean-fail test rejected step 1 because that step itself carries a mechanics signal.

rows.rationale: SOLE CATCHER for: a structurally failed planning turn is execution mechanics. Distinct from the termination row because the two blocks are recorded by different machinery -- a termination is a turn DECLARING the step impossible, a planning failure is the turn producing no usable decision at all -- and a router that read only one of them would classify the other as a clean fail and file a finding about an application that was never exercised.
rows.measured: route repair, signalClass execution-mechanics, mechanics [{stepIndex 1, planning-failure}].

rows.rationale: SOLE CATCHER for: a historical cycle block is NOT a mechanics signal. Nothing writes cycle blocks, so only older handoffs carry one, and reading it as mechanics would send an old dead-control run to repair. The signature cell plus a cycle block must therefore route exactly like the signature cell; a router that still pushed 'cycle' would answer repair here.
rows.measured: route stop, signalClass clean-definitive-assertion-fail, failurePoint step 1 with verdictSource assert-value; the cycle block on step 1 contributed no mechanics signal.

rows.rationale: SOLE CATCHER for: a historical stagnation block is NOT a mechanics signal. A dead control ends at a typed limit stop instead of an exhausted ladder, and the ladder's old blocks are read as nothing; a router that still pushed 'stagnation' would answer repair here.
rows.measured: route stop, signalClass clean-definitive-assertion-fail, failurePoint step 1 with verdictSource assert-value; the stagnation block on step 1 contributed no mechanics signal.

rows.rationale: SOLE CATCHER for: a MEMBER-LEVEL mechanics signal, carried by the outcome rather than by any step. Not one step said no; the member ran out of time. A router whose scan looked only at StepEvidence would find nothing here and fall through to the ambiguity arm, filing a finding about an application nobody observed misbehaving. It is also the row that proves failingStepIndex is nullable for a reason -- there is no step to point at.
rows.measured: route repair, signalClass execution-mechanics, mechanics [{stepIndex null, member-timeout}], failingStepIndex null.

rows.rationale: SOLE CATCHER for: cancellation is the SECOND member-level mechanics outcome, and it is a different fact from a timeout -- something stopped the run rather than the run overrunning. Both are in RunStatus and neither is a statement about the application, so a router that enumerated only one would route the other by ambiguity into a finding.
rows.measured: route repair, signalClass execution-mechanics, mechanics [{stepIndex null, member-cancelled}], failingStepIndex null.

rows.rationale: SOLE CATCHER for: MIXED evidence is ambiguity, and ambiguity routes to finding. A FINDING-DIRECTION CELL. It differs from mechanics-termination in exactly one integer -- the termination sits on step 0 instead of on the failing step 1 -- and lands on the opposite arm. A router whose mechanics scan is narrowed to the failing step gives these two rows the same class, which is why this pair, and not any single row, is what pins the scan's width.
rows.measured: route stop, signalClass mixed-evidence; the clean-fail test accepted step 1 (its own step carries no mechanics) while the all-steps scan found a termination on step 0.

rows.rationale: SOLE CATCHER for: a failure with NEITHER a mechanics signal NOR a definitive verdict source is unclassifiable, and unclassifiable is ambiguity. A FINDING-DIRECTION CELL. It is the signature cell with the verdict source removed and nothing else changed, so it is the row that proves the router actually READS verdictSource rather than treating any failed step as definitive -- a router that skipped that field would classify this identically to the signature cell and no other row would notice.
rows.measured: route stop, signalClass indefinitive-failure; step 1's verdict is false and it records no verdictSource, so the definitive test rejects it and the mechanics scan finds nothing.

rows.rationale: SOLE CATCHER for: the router REFUSES rather than inventing a route. There is no failure here to route -- a healed pass is a pass -- and both arms would be a wrong answer wearing a correct one's clothes. This is also the ADMIT-side control for the whole member-outcome axis: mechanics-member-timeout and mechanics-member-cancelled are this row with the outcome changed and nothing else, so a router that answered 'repair' for every member outcome it did not recognise would pass those two rows and fail here.
rows.measured: signalClass no-failure; routing throws AuthoringRouterUnroutableError naming no-failure. Outcome healed with no step verdict false.
